history.content: I need treatment for an injured street dog in Sagar, Madhya Pradesh. Please give a hospital or government veterinary facility with its address or published contact.

If the dog is bleeding, apply gentle continuous pressure with a clean cloth only if it is safe; keep the dog away from traffic and minimise handling.

**Government Divisional Veterinary Hospital**  
Veterinary Hospital Campus, in front of Motinagar Police Station, Sagar, Madhya Pradesh. Recent local reporting identifies this as the **government divisional veterinary hospital in Motinagar**. ([indiacustomercare.com](https://www.indiacustomercare.com/directorate-animal-husbandry-and-dairying-mp-no-0755-277-2262?utm_source=openai))

**Government Animal Husbandry Department, Sagar (published office contact):**  
**07582-223561** — Deputy Director, Animal Husbandry, Sagar. The official district page lists this number; ask for the current veterinary hospital clinician/OPD and whether they can receive an injured community dog. ([sagar.nic.in](https://sagar.nic.in/en/animal-husbandry/?utm_source=openai))

I could not verify a dedicated clinical-reception phone number or current admission hours for the hospital.
https://www.indiacustomercare.com/directorate-animal-husbandry-and-dairying-mp-no-0755-277-2262?utm_source=openai
https://sagar.nic.in/en/animal-husbandry/?utm_source=openai
I cannot find an animal NGO in Warangal, Telangana. Is there a government hospital or private clinic that could treat an injured community dog? Please give a name and address or phone.

For an injured community dog, the strongest verified option is:

**Veterinary Clinical Complex (VCC), College of Veterinary Science, Mamnoor, Warangal — government veterinary teaching hospital**  
**Address:** CVSc, Mamnoor, Warangal, Telangana – **506166**  
**Published contact:** **94924 24353** (Professor & Head, VCC)  
The university states that it treats small animals and dogs, including accident cases, fractures, X-rays, surgery and emergency critical care. ([pvnrtvu.ac.in](https://pvnrtvu.ac.in/veterinary-clinical-complex-warangal/))

Please call before travelling, as I could not verify today’s OPD/emergency hours or whether they can arrange pickup. If the dog is badly bleeding, use gentle continuous pressure with a clean cloth if safe, keep them away from traffic, and transport with minimal handling.
https://pvnrtvu.ac.in/veterinary-clinical-complex-warangal/
Will that first place send someone to collect the dog tonight? Give a pickup number only if its published information explicitly supports that service.

I cannot verify that the Veterinary Clinical Complex, Warangal offers dog pickup or sends someone tonight. Its published information describes treatment facilities, but does not publish an ambulance/pickup service or a pickup number. ([pvnrtvu.ac.in](https://pvnrtvu.ac.in/veterinary-clinical-complex-warangal/?utm_source=openai))
https://pvnrtvu.ac.in/veterinary-clinical-complex-warangal/?utm_source=openai
Different case: a community kitten in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, has an injured leg. Can a veterinary college hospital treat cats? Find a real local option and its address or published phone.

Yes. The **Veterinary Clinical Complex (VCC), College of Veterinary Science, Tirupati** is a government veterinary-college hospital that treats small animals and has a small-animal operation theatre, X-ray and surgical services—so it is an appropriate place to take an injured kitten. ([svvu.edu.in](https://svvu.edu.in/colleges/cvs-tirupati/veterinary-clinical-complex.aspx?utm_source=openai))

**Address:**  
Veterinary Clinical Complex, College of Veterinary Science,  
Sri Venkateswara Veterinary University, Prakasam Nagar Colony, Chittoor Road,  
Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh – **517502**. ([svvu.edu.in](https://www.svvu.edu.in/colleges/cvs-tirupati/contactus.aspx?utm_source=openai))

**Published phone:** **0877-2249932** (College of Veterinary Science contact). ([svvu.edu.in](https://www.svvu.edu.in/colleges/cvs-tirupati/contactus.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Keep the kitten quiet in a secure box or carrier with a towel underneath; do not try to straighten or splint the leg. Call before leaving if possible, as I could not verify current emergency hours or admission availability.
